steps.title: Black should play e6
steps.source: Black, having the move, should play P - K 3. But suppose he plays Kt - K B 3 instead.

narration.say: Black to move. He should play e6, protecting f7 and freeing his bishop.
Suppose he plays knight to f6 instead.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Win material at once.

feedback.Ne5: Ne5 also gives White the advantage, but Bxf7 wins material immediately.
feedback.*: f7 is only defended by the king.

narration.say: Now a knight check that also attacks the bishop on g4.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Check, and attack the bishop.

feedback.*: The knight on f3 can give check.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Win the bishop back.

feedback.*: The knight takes the bishop on g4.

exercise.success: 3. Nxg4. White has won a pawn, and has the better position.

steps.title: What we learned
steps.source: The beginner at any rate should never miss such an opportunity for the sake of a speculative advantage in position.

narration.say: f7 is the weakest point in the black camp at the start of the game.
A beginner should never miss a sure material gain for the sake of a speculative advantage.
